patch_description: The current single hexagonal-lattice start confines the search to one basin. Add a set of four structurally diverse deterministic seeds (hex rows 5-4-5-4-5-3, hex rows 4-5-4-5-4-4, a dense 5-column square-like grid with 26 circles in 6 rows, and a corner-anchored layout with 4 large corner circles surrounding a 5-4-5-4 interior lattice). Each seed is LP-evaluated, then the hill-climb is run on the best seed(s) with a per-seed iteration budget, keeping the global best. This exploits the fact that n=26 optimal packings are known to be non-lattice arrangements (the AlphaEvolve solution is irregular), so diverse geometric starts (especially corner-heavy ones where corner circles can grow large due to three-sided slack) give the LP-driven hill-climb access to better basins. Time budget: ~450 LP solves total (~3s at observed 0.006s per LP), well within limits.
